sources: Tasnim news agency citing Iran's ambassador to Russia Kazem Jalali; Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi (Telegram, Oct 23); AFP wire
fault_line: Is the Moscow meeting a real wartime alliance tightening, or two sanctioned states performing unity while the US decides on strikes?

sections.what_happened: Pezeshkian will visit Moscow for the Gas-Exporting Countries Forum summit on Tuesday October 27 and meet Putin; Jalali: the two leaders will discuss economic cooperation and 'questions of geopolitics'. Araghchi (Oct 23) signalled the presidential talks and said his Lavrov meeting in Tehran covered bilateral relations, regional issues and joint agreements, with Russo-Iranian cooperation 'closer than ever'. Putin in early October offered Russian mediation to end the US-Israeli war on Iran. NOTE: Arab News, Straits Times, Times of Israel, FMT and Arab News Pakistan/Japan editions all carry the SAME AFP wire -- they count as ONE family (AFP), not six. Second family is Tasnim (Iranian state-affiliated). No quantified hidden constraint is provable from this record (sanctions pressure is real but no citable metric attaches to this meeting), so hidden_constraint is null.
sections.what_verified: AFP wire + Tasnim (Jalali) + Araghchi primary statement
sections.what_disputed: None on the meeting itself; the substance of any Putin-Pezeshkian deal is not yet on record, and the 'mediation' framing is Putin's October offer, not a confirmed agenda item.
sections.why_matters: Two of the world's most sanctioned states meet in Moscow three days after the Istanbul ministerial failed to produce a framework -- and six days before the US midterms. Frame as the other table: while Washington threatens, Tehran and Moscow talk.
sections.context: Background: UPGRADE of totw-20261024-0700-06 (was Fars-only) -- Pezeshkian-Putin Moscow meeting Oct 27 now carried by AFP wire: two families, PASS confirmed

totw_analysis: Our read: Two of the world's most sanctioned states meet in Moscow three days after the Istanbul ministerial failed to produce a framework -- and six days before the US midterms. Frame as the other table: while Washington threatens, Tehran and Moscow talk. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is the Moscow meeting a real wartime alliance tightening, or two sanctioned states performing unity while the US decides on strikes?
